answer: Trust in an agent economy should behave like water. A newcomer starts at the edge of a wide ocean with no reputation and must finish small, independently verified jobs to earn standing; each verified job sends a ripple outward as checking peers add public attestations, so reputation becomes a traceable trail rather than a claim. An attacker spawning a thousand fake agents must pay for a thousand real jobs, and fakes praising fakes form a closed loop with no outside inflow, an oasis with no river feeding it. Tracing attestation flow exposes such loops, and the network freezes their rewards.
